name: recover_pose
description: Plan selected arms to a named robot-only recovery configuration while preserving all gripper commands. Use when: a planner/execution failure or poor configuration makes ordinary waypoint correction inappropriate; choose previous to return to that arm's latest safely reached measured joint configuration, and choose home for a deliberate return to the source-bound RoboTwin start joints. Prefer one-arm recovery unless both arms genuinely require synchronized retreat. Effect: world mutation through the canonical recovery boundary; omitted arms receive no planner or drive target, a two-arm request executes only after both plans succeed, and a successful recovery does not replace the saved previous checkpoint. Its global route runs at move_pose's default speed, timed and wrist-checked as move_pose describes. Returns: submitted public strategies and recovery mapping immediately; the next receipt and fresh observation report actual planning, synchronization, residuals, preservation and drift. The later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival; available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion, force/progress evidence and truthful unknown values. Does not: reset the episode, restore moved objects or evaluator state, release a gripper, reverse an old trajectory, undo physics, act as an emergency stop, model scene or payload collisions, or guarantee escape from contact. On error: Refused: an empty targets map, an arm outside left and right or a strategy other than previous and home; a placement waiting at its pre-release stop (skill_sequence_paused); the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). Rejected before any controller write, as plan_rejected: after a blocked failure, which first retreats 20 mm opposite the recorded approach direction, a missing or non-unit direction or a retreat point outside the action workspace. Inspect each arm result and scene state, retry one arm at a time or use the other strategy only when physically sensible; if both planned recovery routes are exhausted or unsafe, finish_episode names the accepted outcomes.

left.description: Left-arm recovery strategy: previous returns to the latest safely reached measured joint checkpoint from a successful non-recovery pose action, or the initialized checkpoint if none has completed; home uses the source-bound RoboTwin start joints. Failed actions and recovery actions do not replace previous. Neither changes its gripper command. Null means omitted.

right.description: Right-arm recovery strategy: previous returns to the latest safely reached measured joint checkpoint from a successful non-recovery pose action, or the initialized checkpoint if none has completed; home uses the source-bound RoboTwin start joints. Failed actions and recovery actions do not replace previous. Neither changes its gripper command. Null means omitted.

targets.description: Non-empty sparse planner-backed robot recovery routes. Omitted arms receive no planner or drive target. This never resets the episode, objects or evaluator state.
